sections.heading: Should a 20-Year-Old Roof Be Replaced? Roof Repair vs. Roof Replacement

runs.v: Often, if it is 3-tab asphalt: 3-tab shingles last about 20 years and architectural shingles about 30, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, so a 20-year-old 3-tab roof with curling or missing shingles, granule loss, or leaks at more than one spot is due. A 20-year-old slate, metal, or copper roof is usually mid-life and needs roof repair to its flashing and fasteners instead. Roofs typically last 15-20 years before needing repairs, and West Orange roofs often require replacement after 15-20 years. Roof repairs prevent severe problems affecting your home, and a focused repair addresses identifiable defects in roofs, but widespread leaks often indicate the need for replacement, and a roof replacement can resolve recurring leak issues that patching cannot. Most residential roof replacements take one to two days, longer for slate or a rotted deck, and a new roof can increase a home's value and protection.

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Replace a roof when damage exceeds 25 to 30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, and repair when the damage stays localized on an asphalt roof under 10 to 15 years old; the area and cost rules are contractor-consensus thresholds, per published NJ contractor pricing and Modernize cost guidance, and a localized repair can cost 5 to 10 times less than replacement, per Home Depot cost data. New Jersey's code draws a matching line for permits: on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, work on more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months needs a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.
